column3: The Hebrew says he prepared his seat; BSB says he took his seat.
The Hebrew says the young men hid themselves; BSB says they withdrew.
The Hebrew has a singular voice and tongue; BSB has plural voices and tongues.
The Hebrew makes an ear and an eye the subjects of hearing and seeing; BSB speaks of people who heard and saw.
The Hebrew makes the dying person’s blessing the subject that came upon him; BSB says the dying man blessed him.
The Hebrew speaks of investigating the case of someone he did not know; BSB says he took up the stranger’s case.
The Hebrew names jaws and casting prey from his teeth; BSB names fangs and snatching the prey.
The Hebrew has a singular root opened toward water; BSB has plural roots spreading out.
The Hebrew says his speech dripped upon them without explicitly naming dew; BSB supplies the comparison with dew.
The Hebrew says they opened their mouth wide for late rain; BSB describes drinking in his words like spring showers.
The Hebrew says they did not cause the light of his face to fall; BSB says that light was precious.
